problem: The HTTP outer callback closed sockets after a successful upgrade callback returned, preventing transferred owners from sending later frames.
implementation: Retain transferred sockets in the upgraded ownership set until transport close or service unload; ordinary connection bookkeeping remains until its close waiter settles. Preserve upstream half-open behavior. Correct the reset regression to close a raw SO_LINGER peer without Proactor's preceding shutdown, and update the Connection fixture to the existing atomic modifyRecord interface.

paired.scope: Original and Native plain/TLS returned callbacks answer two later frames; plain peer FIN preserves the owner's write half; unload closes all sockets and settles owner jobs.

connection_pair.scope: Original RecordCredentials and Native equivalent: actual HTTP authentication, middleware, RPC, unload/reload, credential persistence and recovery injection.

native.scope: Transferred upgrade, TLS, ordinary/upgrade real peer RST, connection lifetime and WebServer consumers.

consumers.scope: Connection plugin/trust, duplex mux, resource HTTP and Gateway write/close consumers.

diagnostics: rc022-upgrade-owner-before-pair-20261117-01: pre-fix Native returned EOF after 101, while Original answered later frames.
rc022-upgrade-owner-native-20261117-01 and consumers-20261117-01 retain original reset-test and obsolete fixture failures.
rc022-upgrade-owner-pair2-20261117-01: experimental EOF-close assumption rejected by Original timeout. The production EOF change was removed; final explicit half-open pairing passed.

cleanup.scope: All owned initial/final targeted workspaces, homes and temporary directories; logs, XML, Source and paired observations retained.

limitations: Targeted ownership verification only; production pin promotion, full release qualification and actual Windows 7 acceptance remain separate.
